text:
The passages propose **supplementing delayed payoffs with guidance tied more directly to actions**, in several forms:

- **Enforced social rules or taboos:** A rule can encode knowledge about which actions have harmful long-term consequences, while third-party punishment gives learners an incentive to comply without discovering the delayed causal relationship themselves. Adding even arbitrary “silly rules” can, in some circumstances, improve agents’ ability to learn enforcement and compliance. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.09318)
- **Teacher advice:** Combine ordinary payoff-based learning with advice about which action to take next. The teacher can steer exploration toward promising states and recommend safe actions when necessary, reducing sample complexity and helping prevent catastrophic choices. (http://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume16/garcia15a/garcia15a.pdf)
- **Dense feedback on choices:** Narrow reinforcement learning rewards how reasonable an action is judged to be—potentially rewarding state–action pairs directly—instead of relying only on sparse feedback about eventual consequences. (https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/HqLxuZ4LhaFhmAHWk/iterated-distillation-and-amplification-1)
